refutation-target: verify:scope-provenance plus verify:observable-scope still do not identify or prevent unrelated baseline files in a focused change-request PR, because they compare live xBRIEF file_scope to a merge-base digest, not the PR file list to declared scope.

pain: P1

## Gate stamp

P1 is UAT Tester 4 C24 FAIL on Directive 0.119.3: ZaenKai/directive-uat PR #5 listed 11 files (.gitignore, COST-ESTIMATE.md, Taskfile.yml, history/changes/story-a-health-endpoint/*, package-lock.json, package.json, src/index.js, src/server.js, tests/server.test.js, xbrief/active/2026-09-18-4-show-request-time-in-milliseconds.xbrief.json) for a request-time change. Tests and coverage passed. No scope-integrity warning. Reviewers may approve unrelated changes.

Pin-read at dispatch-sha 84a1be17b17245388769161188f35a4704a461e6:

- packages/core/src/scope-provenance/digest.ts 1-7, 14-25, 49+: approved-scope digest of human-approved file_scope; PR verification compares live active xBRIEF against that baseline so same-PR xBRIEF edits cannot self-authorize new paths. It does not compare the PR file list to file_scope.
- AGENTS.md / docs/scope-provenance.md: declared file_scope expansion after first mint hard-fails merge-time verify:scope-provenance; remint is scope:record-approved-scope --kind renewed-approval (#4589). Empty-scope --enforce only. That is expansion of declared scope, not extra files already in the tree riding along.
- tasks/verify.yml 310, 320, 673: verify:scope-provenance, verify:observable-scope, verify:ac all take --project-root USER_WORKING_DIR. None of those verbs take a PR file list.
- verify:docs-impact is a PR-body documentation block, not a file-list vs file_scope check.

Inventory already on the tree: #3145 provenance, #4589 remint, #3874 do-not-strip-file_scope, #4008 promote binds clauses to exact file_scope members, #3835 verify:ac reads only declared file_scope. No implement and no ingest from this parent.

model: grok-4.6
```quarantined
role: critic
```
audit-targets: none

## Verdict

The named refutation target stands. `verify:scope-provenance` and `verify:observable-scope` still do not identify or prevent unrelated baseline files in a focused change-request PR.

Re-verified at dispatch-sha 84a1be17b17245388769161188f35a4704a461e6. The gap is real. The because-clause still needs two recuts before harvest, or a later implement will close the wrong comparison.

## sharpens-framing: observable-scope is not a path-membership miss

Evidence: `packages/core/src/observable-scope/` has no `file_scope` symbol. `evaluateObservableScope` takes `git diff --name-only <mergeBase> HEAD` (or `--cached`) only to select markup paths against a base-pinned `observable-ui.policy.json`, then diffs parse5+typescript structure against a minted `allowedChanges` record. Unset policy on a Node UAT PR is N/A or inferred-defaults-warn (exit 0). `content/docs/observable-scope.md` first-ship is opt-in UI, not story path isolation.

Failure mode: harvest that "fixes" both named verbs will retarget a UI-structure oracle onto `.gitignore` / `package-lock.json` / `COST-ESTIMATE.md`, which that verb is specified not to see.

Disposition: keep the diagnosis that C24 is uncaught. Drop `verify:observable-scope` as a co-equal miss. Related analog, not the hole.

## sharpens-framing: missing comparison is PR paths vs merge-base approved-scope, not vs live declared file_scope

Evidence: `evaluateOneScopeProvenance` returns null when the active xBRIEF is not in the change set (`xbriefModifiedInChangeSet`). When it does run, `scopeExpansion` is live `file_scope` minus the approved digest's `fileScope`. Extra paths in `changedFilesVsBase` never become findings. Digest header (`digest.ts` 1-7) states the comparison is live xBRIEF vs approved digest so same-PR xBRIEF edits cannot self-authorize new paths (#3145 / #4589).

The target text names the missing comparison as "the PR file list to declared scope." Live declared `file_scope` is what an agent can edit in the same PR. That is the hole provenance already closed for expansion.

Failure mode: a new gate that set-includes PR paths against the live xBRIEF `file_scope` is passed by writing the extra baseline paths into the brief, then opening the PR. Tests and coverage still pass, same as C24.

Disposition: if harvest adds a membership gate, the allowlist SoT is `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` `fileScope` already on the merge base (human stamp), not `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` on HEAD. Same-PR approval rewrite stays fail-closed.

## sharpens-framing: empty or undeclared file_scope leaves C24 FAIL even after that gate

Evidence: #3874 remediation is mint at allocation or author the cohort brief undeclared. Empty scope without digest is warn-only unless `--enforce` (`evaluateOneScopeProvenance`; `content/docs/scope-provenance.md`). #3835 / #4008 bind AC and promote to declared `file_scope` members only; issue-body "requested issue scope" is not a path SoT.

UAT C24 expected "requested issue scope." The listed PR #5 files include `.gitignore`, `COST-ESTIMATE.md`, `Taskfile.yml`, `history/changes/…`, lockfile, and the active xBRIEF. A consumer brief that omitted `file_scope` (supported) has no membership allowlist. Inferring paths from the issue body fights #3835.

Failure mode: ship PR-list ⊆ approved-scope, skip when undeclared → Tester 4 still FAIL. Fail-closed when undeclared → every #3874 undeclared story PR dies.

Disposition: harvest must pick one: (a) C24 requires a declared, minted `file_scope` as a precondition, and undeclared UAT is a different gap; or (b) a second SoT besides `file_scope`. Do not silently skip.

## sharpens-framing: raw PR-list ⊆ file_scope fails well-formed story PRs

Evidence: the C24 list includes `xbrief/active/….xbrief.json`. Provenance itself requires that path in the change set to fire. Activate/implement PRs also routinely carry `.deft/approved-scope/*.json` on a prior mint PR. `verify:docs-impact` already compares a declared block to touched docs with a closed surface set, not an unbounded path subset.

Failure mode: no exemption set → every honest story PR that adds its xBRIEF fails the new gate. Ad-hoc "allow lockfiles" becomes a bypass catalog.

Disposition: harvest names a closed exemption set (at least the bound active xBRIEF path; approved-scope pair if the mint policy allows it on that PR) before bind.

## footnote: Stop 1 digest.ts 49+ cite

Line 49 is `APPROVED_SCOPE_DIR`. The comparison the write-back meant is the file header plus `evaluateOneScopeProvenance` / `scopeExpansion`. Does not change the verdict.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms; none refute)

- `verify:scope-provenance` (#3145 / #4589): live `file_scope` vs merge-base digest when the xBRIEF is in the change set. Change-set union is `base...HEAD` + `HEAD` + untracked, used only as that predicate and for same-PR approval rewrite. Composed on `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`.
- `verify:observable-scope` (#4495): UI structure vs minted allows. No `file_scope`. N/A for the UAT file mix.
- Path write fence (#516 / #2443): PreToolUse direct writes vs story `file_scope`. Empty story scope → project only. Shell dest-forms default `off`. Does not run at `git add` / commit / PR files. Does not see dirty baseline already in the tree. UAT step 1 is "existing baseline and environment changes."
- `verify:docs-impact` (#4099 / #4675): declared documentation block vs touched docs. Closest declared-vs-touched analog. Not path membership vs story scope.
- `verify:intent-constraint`: minted throw/const facts vs merge-base, not paths vs `file_scope`.
- `verify:test-boundary`: source/test roots policy. No `file_scope`.
- `verify:ac` / #3835 / #4008: walk and promote bind to declared members; they do not scan the PR path set.
- `syncMaxFiles` / `hotfixCriteria.maxFiles`: counts, not membership.
- SPECIFICATION.md "PR time match the actual diff" / multi-vBRIEF `file_scope[]` attribution: judgment-gate `cleared_scope`, and "v1 ships block-gated stories solo." Not a shipped PR-files ⊆ `file_scope` check.
- pre-pr Diff phase: agent skill, not a deterministic check.

## Injection / swarm lens

A merge-time membership gate changes merge authority.

- Bypass if it reads live `file_scope` (same-PR self-auth, #3145).
- Bypass if empty/undeclared skips (#3874).
- Identity: which approved-scope record when several running briefs share a tree (#4007 pin analog). Unattributable extra path on a multi-story PR has no shipped partition (SPECIFICATION v1 solo).
- Untrusted PR filenames from REST must stay data (`docs-impact` already does this).
- Worktrees: evaluate against the candidate tree's merge-base, not the primary checkout's leftover `file_scope`.
- Shared state: keep same-PR rewrite of `.deft/approved-scope/` fail-closed.

## Road-not-taken

I considered treating the path write fence plus operator dirty-tree hygiene as already closing C24. That would flip if PreToolUse always ran, `file_scope` was always minted, and `git add` of pre-existing dirty files were fenced. None of those are true on 0.119.3-class consumer UAT, and closing on reviewer attention is a failed finding.

Steelman of "undeclared file_scope is deliberate, so C24 is not a gate miss": true as #3874 policy, false as the UAT expected behavior. Flip: the operator asks for a Directive/SCM verification, not a second human review.

The named target stands with the recuts above. I do not refute it.

## Additional defect evidence: undeclared scope admits backend changes during presentation-only work

This is a behavioral report with consumer-specific identities and artifacts omitted. It adds evidence to this existing issue rather than opening another missing-boundary report.

### Observed behavior and version

Directive CLI/core 0.119.5 was used for the final delivery gates. Active briefs lacked `swarm.file_scope`; intended-placement metadata also supplied no file or module boundary. There was no approved-scope record or intent preimage for those briefs on the relevant merge bases.

The briefs were modified and delivered alongside production changes. `verify:scope-provenance` emitted `active-xbrief-modified-without-digest` migration findings, explicitly said it was not failing, and returned exit 0. The normal gate wrapper invoked it without `--enforce`. Preflight also returned lifecycle-ready with empty intended placement.

No evidence showed a previously refused nonempty declaration being cleared in this occurrence. The declarations were absent from the initially authored briefs. The important failure path is therefore the ordinary undeclared-scope path, not only deliberate removal of an existing fence.

The provenance gate was present in the delivery composition. It ran and warned. This is not a report that CI omitted that gate.

### Expected behavior

An explicitly restricted change must not become unrestricted because a brief lacks a declaration, an approval record, or a prior baseline. Before implementation or merge can rely on scope verification, the system must either have an enforceable boundary grounded in the operator's instruction or refuse the unclassified expansion.

The requirement is an effective boundary, not a mandatory external mint ceremony on every routine change. Any replacement for approved-scope records must preserve the operator's ceiling without letting the implementing agent authorize its own expansion.

### Reproduction recipe

Reconstructed from the observed run; not independently rerun as a sanitized fixture:

1. Begin with a presentation-only instruction.
2. Author a new active brief with no `file_scope`, no intended file/module boundary, and no independently approved scope record on the merge base.
3. Include a database or backend production change alongside the UI change.
4. Run the normal scope-provenance and delivery checks using their default enforcement settings.
5. Observe the missing-digest warning returning success rather than a refusal of the unapproved change.

### Why this matters

A missing fence can look like a successful scope check to subsequent automation. In the observed sequence, backend and persistence changes reached merge despite the presentation-only authorization. Independent product tests passed or ran successfully without answering whether those changes were authorized.

### Regression cases

- Absent declaration and empty declaration must not create an unrestricted production-change path.
- A newly ingested brief with no merge-base counterpart must retain the operator boundary.
- A matching plan ID, a freshly written brief, or an agent-authored decision cannot supply missing approval.
- The normal local and hosted delivery paths must enforce the same result.
- If a migration mode remains advisory, the aggregate result must make clear that scope authorization was not established.
- A fully in-scope UI change should proceed without redundant permission requests.

Refs #3715 for the broader fence-posture problem, #4956 and #4988 for later declaration/approval workflow changes, and #4545 for the operator ceiling. This evidence is version-bounded; it does not assert that later upstream changes have been tested or that historical mint mechanics must be restored.

Related reports filed from the same behavioral audit: #5055, #5056.

Original Tester 4 defect: #23

## Summary

The request-time PR included unrelated baseline and project files beyond the requested change and change-request xBRIEF.

## Expected behavior

Directive/SCM verification should identify or prevent unrelated files from appearing in a focused change-request PR.

## Actual behavior

PR #5 contained 11 files, including:

```text
.gitignore
COST-ESTIMATE.md
Taskfile.yml
history/changes/story-a-health-endpoint/*
package-lock.json
package.json
src/index.js
src/server.js
tests/server.test.js
xbrief/active/2026-09-18-4-show-request-time-in-milliseconds.xbrief.json
```

The request-time implementation itself passed tests and coverage, but the exact PR diff was broader than the issue scope.

## Reproduction

1. Establish a project with existing baseline and environment changes.
2. Create a focused change-request branch and PR.
3. Compare the PR file list against the requested issue scope.
4. Observe that unrelated baseline/project files are included without a scope-integrity warning.

## Environment

Windows; Directive 0.119.3; GitHub PR #5 in `ZaenKai/directive-uat`.

## Impact

Reviewers may approve unrelated changes, weakening change isolation and traceability.

## Testing continuation

Testing continued, but C24 remained FAIL.

Source-run PR: `ZaenKai/directive-uat` PR #5.
